title: Time Bender
blurb: History's dates are messing with you. Three are real, one is cap. Trust nothing.

cards.say: Harvard University [was founded before anyone had invented calculus], [held its first graduation, for nine students, the year Galileo died], [was founded before the playwright William Shakespeare died], and [is named after a minister who left it his library].
cards.real: Shakespeare died in 1616. Harvard was founded 20 years later, in 1636, by a vote of the Massachusetts Bay Colony's legislature.
src: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_Harvard_University (founded 1636) + https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_calculus (developed by Newton, 1664 to 1666, and Leibniz, from 1675)
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_Harvard_University (first commencement 1642, nine students) + https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Galileo_Galilei (died 8 January 1642)
https://www.britannica.com/biography/William-Shakespeare (died April 23, 1616) + https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_Harvard_University (founded 1636 by vote of the Great and General Court)
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_Harvard_University (the Puritan clergyman John Harvard willed it his library of some 400 books; named Harvard College in 1639)

cards.say: The Ottoman Empire [still existed when Mickey Mouse first appeared in a cartoon], [lasted for more than six centuries], [conquered Constantinople almost 40 years before Columbus sailed], and [still existed when the Wright brothers first flew].
cards.real: The Ottoman sultanate was abolished in November 1922, six years before Mickey Mouse's first cartoons came out in 1928.
src: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ottoman_Empire (sultanate abolished 1 November 1922) + https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steamboat_Willie (1928)
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ottoman_Empire (founded c. 1299, sultanate abolished 1922) + https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_the_Ottoman_Empire
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ottoman_Empire (Constantinople conquered 29 May 1453) + https://www.britannica.com/biography/Christopher-Columbus/The-first-voyage (1492)
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ottoman_Empire (sultanate abolished 1 November 1922) + https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wright_brothers (first flight December 17, 1903)

cards.say: Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart [is younger than America's Liberty Bell], [wrote music for a glass instrument invented by Benjamin Franklin], [was still alive when George Washington became president], and [wrote the tune of Twinkle Twinkle Little Star at age five].
cards.real: The tune came from an unknown French composer around 1765. Mozart wrote variations on it in Vienna in 1781 or 1782, when he was in his twenties.
src: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liberty_Bell (commissioned 1752, arrived August 1752, recast by June 1753) + https://www.themorgan.org/exhibitions/online/mozart/418 (Mozart 1756-1791)

https://www.parlancechamberconcerts.org/individual-program-notes/wolfgang-amadeus-mozart-(1756-1791)/adagio-in-c-for-armonica,-k.-617 (Adagio in C for solo armonica, 1791; Franklin designed the instrument)

https://www.parlancechamberconcerts.org/individual-program-notes/wolfgang-amadeus-mozart-(1756-1791)/adagio-in-c-for-armonica,-k.-617 (Mozart 1756-1791) + https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Washington (inaugurated April 30, 1789)
https://www.themorgan.org/exhibitions/online/mozart/418 (variations K. 265 written in Vienna 1781-1782 on a tune by an unknown composer from around 1765)

cards.say: Marie Curie [was born the same year the United States bought Alaska], [won her second Nobel Prize after World War I ended], [won her first Nobel Prize the same year the Wright brothers first flew], and [set up mobile X-ray units for soldiers in World War I].
cards.real: Curie's second Nobel Prize, in chemistry, came in 1911, three years before World War I began. She was the first person ever to win two.
src: https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/physics/1903/marie-curie/facts (born 7 November 1867) + https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alaska_Purchase (treaty signed March 30, 1867)

https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/physics/1903/marie-curie/facts (Physics prize 1903) + https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wright_brothers (first flight December 17, 1903)
https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/physics/1903/marie-curie/facts (organized mobile X-ray teams in World War I)

cards.say: Charles Darwin [was born on the very same day as Abraham Lincoln], [died before Alexander Graham Bell patented the telephone], [ate puma, armadillo and iguana on his voyage around the world], and [published his theory of evolution before the US Civil War began].
cards.real: Bell patented the telephone in 1876. Darwin lived six more years and died in April 1882.
src: https://clarklibrary.ucla.edu/blog/charles-darwin-abraham-lincoln-and-the-12th-of-february/ (both born 12 February 1809)
https://darwin-online.org.uk/converted/Ancillary/1882_RGSobituary_A118.html (died 19 April 1882) + https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexander_Graham_Bell (patent 174,465 issued March 7, 1876)
https://www.nhpr.org/npr-blogs/2015-08-12/dining-like-darwin-when-scientists-swallow-their-subjects (puma, armadillos and iguanas on the Beagle voyage)
https://clarklibrary.ucla.edu/blog/charles-darwin-abraham-lincoln-and-the-12th-of-february/ (On the Origin of Species, 1859; the Civil War began April 1861)

cards.say: Apple [was founded before the first Star Wars movie came out], [was founded closer in time to the Moon landing than to the first iPhone], [had a third co-founder who sold his 10 percent share for 800 dollars], and [got its start a year before its rival Microsoft did].
cards.real: Microsoft was founded in April 1975 in Albuquerque, New Mexico, a year before Apple started on April 1, 1976.
src: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apple_Inc. (founded April 1, 1976; Star Wars opened May 25, 1977)

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_Microsoft (founded April 4, 1975, in Albuquerque)

cards.say: Nokia [made the world's first mobile phone call, back in 1973], [started out as a pulp mill before the telephone was even invented], [was once the third-biggest TV maker in Europe], and [got its classic ringtone from a guitar piece written before the first airplane flight].
cards.real: The first handheld cell phone call was made by Martin Cooper of Motorola in 1973. Nokia's first mobile phone, the Mobira Senator car phone, came in 1982.
src: https://www.aarp.org/politics-society/history/info-2018/first-cell-phone-call.html (Motorola's Martin Cooper, April 3, 1973) + https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nokia (Mobira Senator, Nokia's first mobile phone, 1982)
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nokia (pulp mill founded 1865) + https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexander_Graham_Bell (telephone patent 1876)
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nokia (late-1980s TV maker purchases made Nokia the third-largest television manufacturer of Europe)
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nokia_tune (Tarrega's Gran Vals, 1902; the Wright brothers first flew December 1903)

cards.say: The Mongol Empire [was founded nine years before England's Magna Carta], [is about a century older than the Ottoman Empire], [took control of Japan after invading it a second time in 1281], and [had relay riders who carried mail up to 190 miles in a day].
cards.real: The Mongols invaded Japan in 1274 and 1281 and failed both times. In 1281 a huge typhoon wrecked much of their fleet.
src: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mongol_Empire (a kurultai proclaimed Temujin khan in 1206; Magna Carta was sealed in 1215)

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mongol_Empire (Kublai invaded in 1274 and 1281 and was not able to conquer Japan) + https://www.thecollector.com/why-mongol-invasions-of-japan-failed/ (August 1281 typhoon)
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yam_(route) (messengers covered 200 to 300 km, 120 to 190 miles, per day; Weatherford 2005)

cards.say: Galileo Galilei [was born the same year as William Shakespeare], [was still alive when the Pilgrims landed at Plymouth], [has one of his fingers on display in a museum in Florence], and [built the world's very first telescope in 1608].
cards.real: A Dutch eyeglass maker, Hans Lippershey, tried to patent a telescope in 1608. Galileo heard about it and built his own better one in 1609.
src: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Galileo_Galilei (born 15 February 1564) + https://www.britannica.com/biography/William-Shakespeare (baptized April 26, 1564)
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Galileo_Galilei (died 8 January 1642; the Mayflower Pilgrims landed in 1620)
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Galileo%27s_middle_finger (in the Museo Galileo collection, Florence)
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Galileo_Galilei (Lippershey tried to patent a telescope in the Netherlands in 1608; Galileo made his own in 1609)

cards.say: The Beatles [released their first single on the day the first James Bond movie premiered], [hit number one in Britain with their very first single], [gave their final public performance before the first Moon landing], and [had the police come up to stop their final show].
cards.real: Love Me Do, their first single, came out in October 1962 and peaked at number 17 on the UK chart.

cards.say: Johann Sebastian Bach [was born the same year as the composer Handel], [died less than six years before Mozart was born], [was born after Isaac Newton published his laws of motion], and [had 20 children with his two wives].
cards.real: Bach was born in March 1685. Newton's Principia, with his laws of motion, came out two years later, in July 1687.
src: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Frideric_Handel (born in 1685, the same year as Johann Sebastian Bach)

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Isaac_Newton (Principia published 5 July 1687) + https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johann_Sebastian_Bach (born 31 March 1685)

cards.say: Jackie Robinson [broke baseball's color line before World War II ended], [played his first Dodgers game before the US Air Force existed], [won the first Rookie of the Year award baseball ever handed out], and [had his number 42 retired by every MLB team in 1997].
cards.real: World War II ended in 1945. Robinson, who served in the Army during the war, played his first game for the Brooklyn Dodgers on April 15, 1947.
